name: Longhorn Beetle Infestation
symptoms: Holes and tunnels in stems, branches, or trunks Frass (sawdust-like excrement) around entry holes Wilting or yellowing of leaves Dieback of branches Stunted growth
description: Longhorn beetles are wood-boring insects that attack trees and woody plants. Larvae bore into stems and trunks, weakening plants and causing structural damage, sometimes leading to death of the host.
management: Inspect and remove infested wood Prune and destroy affected branches Monitor adult beetle populations with traps Promote tree health to reduce susceptibility Avoid transporting firewood or plant material from infested areas
prevention: Quarantine and inspect imported wood and nursery plants Maintain vigorous tree health Remove dead or stressed trees promptly Use tree wraps or protective barriers where feasible
